name: Uncrossing white vertices on a W-spider
summary: Between the legs of two labelled white vertices on a W-spider, a fermionic crossing is an ordinary swap.
description:
The *crossing* (fermionic swap) of the ZW-calculus is the map $|00\rangle\langle 00| + |01\rangle\langle 10| + |10\rangle\langle 01| - |11\rangle\langle 11|$: a swap that picks up a sign $-1$ when two $|1\rangle$'s (two fermions) are exchanged. It equals a SWAP followed by a CZ. It behaves like a symmetric braiding, except that it is only natural for *even* maps (those whose terms all have an even number of 1s); maps of odd parity, such as the black vertices, pick up signs. 

Two labelled white vertices (Z-boxes with labels $r$ and $s$) attached to the same W-spider never both carry a $|1\rangle$, since the W-spider spreads a single excitation. So a fermionic crossing between a leg of one and a leg of the other never picks up a sign, and can be replaced by an ordinary swap. This is the labelled analogue of [rule X](../fermionic-crossing-elimination/).
unchecked_reason: uses the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus, which is not a PyZX generator
